idiom_name: sealed trait + case classes with a circe discriminator codec and match dispatch
implementation_notes: Scala's ADT idiom already is the pattern: a sealed trait with case classes is a closed command hierarchy, a derived codec writes the discriminator (io.circe.generic.extras.Configuration.default.withDiscriminator("type") with deriveConfiguredEncoder/Decoder, or Jackson's @JsonTypeInfo), and the invoker matches on the case classes - non-exhaustive matches warn instead of a registry silently missing a type. When commands travel through Akka they are sent to an actor, but Akka disables Java serialization by default (akka.actor.allow-java-serialization = off), so a custom Serializer with a stable numeric identifier, or a protobuf/Avro binding, must be registered for the command trait: the transport does not remove the obligation to have an explicit wire contract.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Command
final case class RenderCommand(reportId: Int) extends Command
case object FlushCommand extends Command

val cfg = Configuration.default.withDiscriminator("type")
implicit val enc: Encoder[Command] = deriveConfiguredEncoder
implicit val dec: Decoder[Command] = deriveConfiguredDecoder

def invoke(envelope: String): Either[Error, Unit] =
  decode[Command](envelope).map {
    case RenderCommand(id) => renderer.render(id)
    case FlushCommand      => flush()
  }
pitfalls: Jackson's default typing (enableDefaultTyping / DefaultTyping.NON_FINAL) resolves class names from the payload and is a gadget vector: prefer the derived circe discriminator or an explicit subtype list and never enable default typing for untrusted envelopes.

The discriminator shape is library-specific - circe wraps the object with the discriminator field while Jackson can inline it as a property - so pick one and pin it, because switching codecs invalidates messages already on the queue.

Akka's Java-serialization-off default means a command trait without a registered serializer fails at send time; a custom Serializer's numeric identifier is part of the wire contract and must not be reordered.
